_readme: Narration script. One entry per segment of the Full cut.
Rule: the narration must NOT read the on-screen caption aloud. Captions
carry the specifics; the voice carries the story between them. Hearing a
sentence you are simultaneously reading is the fastest way to make a demo
open: Running a conference is six spreadsheets, four hundred emails, and a forty thousand dollar tool the customer called slow. Twice. On camera. So here is the same job, start to finish, in one product.
act-Import: It starts the way it always starts. Somebody hands you a spreadsheet.
beat-d-import-2-plan: So hand it straight to StageStack. An agent reads the file, works out what each row is, and writes back a plan.
beat-d-import-record: Every row is accounted for, and nothing touches your event until you say so.
beat-03-cfp-builder: The call for speakers is yours to shape. Sections, questions, what's required.
beat-d-cfp-conditional: And it can ask a workshop something it would never ask a lightning talk.
beat-06-public-cfp: Publish it, and speakers get a form that remembers where they left off.
beat-19-reviewer-scoring: Reviewers get a queue instead of a spreadsheet, and they cannot see whose talk they're scoring.
beat-d-scorecard: You decide once what matters, and every reviewer's score lands on that same scale.
act-Decide: Which makes the decision the easy part.
beat-16-proposals-table: Sort, stage every outcome, and release them together.
beat-12b-comms-log: And every one of them keeps its receipt. This is real mail, with a real calendar invite attached.
beat-40-gmail-invite: That is not a screenshot of our own app. That is a real inbox, and Google has already read the invitation and offered to put it on her calendar.
beat-agenda-drag: Drag a session where you want it. Put two things in one room and it tells you immediately, on both cards, without reloading anything.
beat-agenda-views: And the same program reads five different ways, because the committee, the attendees and you are not looking for the same thing.
act-Prep: Now the part that usually eats your month.
beat-08-speaker-portal: Speakers get their own page, so they stop asking you what they're missing.
beat-d-speaker-slot: They see their slot in their own timezone, and can flag a clash without emailing you.
beat-d-ops-warning: And you get told what's outstanding. Not from a checklist you maintain, but from the data itself.
beat-26-speaker-tasks: The reminders go out on their own.
beat-28-public-event-page: One click, and the program you just built is the program the world sees.
beat-29-embed-widget: On your own site too, with feeds for everything else.
close: StageStack. One event, end to end. Open source, self hostable, and no per-event pricing.
